deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is §§59–60 of the suppressed second part of Ramanujan's 'Highly composite numbers' (1915). Here σ_{-s}(N) = Σ_{d|N} d^{-s} = ∏_{p^a || N} (1 − p^{-s(a+1)})/(1 − p^{-s}), with s > 0. The page studies the 'generalised superior highly composite numbers' (GSHCN) defined on the previous page by (304)–(305). N is GSHCN for ε > 0 if σ_{-s}(N)/N^ε ≥ σ_{-s}(N')/N'^ε for N' < N, with strict inequality for N' > N.

Top of page. A GSHCN has non-increasing exponents a_2 ≥ a_3 ≥ … (from (303)). So it can be written either as 2^{a_2}3^{a_3}⋯p_1^{a_{p_1}} or as a product of primorials (2·3·5⋯p_1)(2·3·5⋯p_2)(2·3·5⋯p_3)⋯. Here p_r is the largest prime whose exponent is ≥ r.

§60, step 1: take N' = N/λ. Here λ is a prime ≤ p_1, so a_λ ≥ 1 (primality is implicit in the manuscript). Only the λ-factor of σ_{-s} changes:
 σ_{-s}(N)/σ_{-s}(N/λ) = (1 − λ^{-s(1+a_λ)})/(1 − λ^{-s a_λ}).
Condition (304) gives σ_{-s}(N)/σ_{-s}(N/λ) ≥ λ^ε. This is (306): λ^ε ≤ (1 − λ^{-s(1+a)})/(1 − λ^{-sa}).

Step 2: take N' = Nλ, valid for any prime λ, including a_λ = 0. Then
 σ_{-s}(Nλ)/σ_{-s}(N) = (1 − λ^{-s(2+a)})/(1 − λ^{-s(1+a)}).
Condition (305) gives that this ratio is < λ^ε. This is (307).

Step 3 (308): put λ = p_1, the largest prime dividing N, so a = 1, in (306). Since (1 − p^{-2s})/(1 − p^{-s}) = 1 + p^{-s}, we get p_1^ε ≤ 1 + p_1^{-s}. Put λ = P_1, the next prime after p_1, so a = 0, in (307); we get P_1^ε > 1 + P_1^{-s}. Hence
 log(1+p_1^{-s})/log p_1 ≥ ε > log(1+P_1^{-s})/log P_1.

Step 4: f(x) = log(1+x^{-s})/log x is strictly decreasing on x > 1 (my justification: the numerator decreases and the denominator increases). So for 0 < ε ≤ f(2), exactly one prime p_1 satisfies (308). For ε > f(2) one would have N = 1 (my remark).

Step 5 (309): solve (306) for a. Put y = λ^{-sa}. Then λ^ε(1 − y) ≤ 1 − λ^{-s}y, i.e. y(λ^ε − λ^{-s}) ≥ λ^ε − 1. Hence λ^{sa} ≤ (λ^ε − λ^{-s})/(λ^ε − 1), i.e.
 a_λ ≤ log((λ^ε − λ^{-s})/(λ^ε − 1))/(s log λ).

Step 6 (310): the same manipulation of (307), with y' = λ^{-s(1+a)}, gives
 1 + a_λ > log((λ^ε − λ^{-s})/(λ^ε − 1))/(s log λ).

The page ends 'From (309) and (310) it is clear that'. The next page concludes (311): a_λ is the integer part of that quantity. This gives an explicit formula for the exponents of a GSHCN in terms of ε, exactly parallel to the formula for superior highly composite numbers in the published part (s → 0 limit) and to the colossally abundant case (s = 1).
errors: No mathematical errors found; the inequalities (306)–(310) are all correct.
Minor implicit assumptions: λ must be prime (written only as 'λ ≤ p_1'). (306) needs a_λ ≥ 1. (309)–(310) need λ^ε > 1, which holds since ε > 0 and λ ≥ 2.
The standard primorial form presupposes the non-increasing exponents from (303). That property is stated earlier for generalised highly composite numbers, and GSHCN are asserted to be such.

results.what: Definition of generalised superior highly composite numbers for σ_{-s}, and their standard form as a product of primorials
results.modern_name: Generalised superior highly composite numbers; for s = 1 these coincide with colossally abundant numbers (σ(n)/n^{1+ε} maximal)
results.usually_credited_to: Alaoglu & Erdős (1944) for colossally abundant numbers; Ramanujan's general σ_{-s} version first published 1997 (Nicolas & Robin, Ramanujan J. 1)

results.what: Local optimality inequalities (306)–(307) obtained by comparing N with N/λ and Nλ
results.modern_name: Standard local-ratio argument for (superior) highly composite / colossally abundant numbers
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (1915, published part, for d(n)); Alaoglu–Erdős (1944) for σ

results.what: Determination of the largest prime p_1 via log(1+p_1^{-s})/log p_1 ≥ ε > log(1+P_1^{-s})/log P_1, and explicit exponent formula a_λ = floor(log((λ^ε−λ^{-s})/(λ^ε−1))/(s log λ))
results.modern_name: Explicit parametrisation of colossally abundant / generalised SHC numbers by ε

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of the suppressed second half of Ramanujan's 'Highly composite numbers' paper. It has been known since its publication with annotations by Nicolas and Robin (1997), and it is widely cited as anticipating Alaoglu–Erdős's colossally abundant numbers. The computations are routine once the definition is set.

checkable.asserts: Ratio σ_{-s}(N)/σ_{-s}(N/λ) equals (1-λ^{-s(1+a)})/(1-λ^{-sa}); the expression simplifies to 1.
With a = 1 (resp. a = 0), the ratios in (306)/(307) reduce to 1 + p^{-s}, giving (308); result is 0.
Boundary y = (λ^ε-1)/(λ^ε-λ^{-s}), i.e. λ^{sa} = (λ^ε-λ^{-s})/(λ^ε-1), the threshold in (309)/(310).
f(x) = log(1+x^{-s})/log x is decreasing at primes for s = 1 (values 0.585, 0.262, 0.113, ...), so p_1 is unique for 0 < ε ≤ f(2).
For s = 1, ε = 0.1 the exponent formula gives a_2, a_3, a_5, a_7; these should match the colossally abundant number for ε = 0.1 and be non-increasing.

checkable.asserts: Brute-force check that the N built from the formula maximises σ_{-1}(n)/n^ε = σ(n)/n^{1+ε} over a range. Replace n0 with the N actually computed from the previous check.

transcription_corrections: In (307) the manuscript writes the inequality as '1 − λ^{-s(1+a_λ)} > {1 − λ^{-s(2+a_λ)}}λ^{-ε}', with the λ^{-ε} placed after the brace, as transcribed.
